title: Runtime research progress conversion loses completed work

failing_environment.runtime_campaign: development scenario originally passed an internal ratio check but direct 3.2.3-to-3.2.5 upgrade proof exposed a redundant second conversion; corrected development and candidate-bound campaigns remain pending

reproduction.observed: The original runtime used an inverse ratio. Its first repair used the mathematically correct old_cost / new_cost ratio, but Factorio had already normalized active research before on_configuration_changed. The second conversion reduced valid completed work in both same-version settings changes and the direct 3.2.3-to-3.2.5 upgrade.

root_cause.summary: The legacy implementation reconstructed costs from a narrow string grammar and applied the inverse ratio. The descriptor repair corrected the algebra but still mutated an engine-normalized value. Runtime descriptors remain useful evidence, but MIR must not reapply Factorio's completed-work conversion.

regression_propositions: fixed linear exponential and hybrid form a complete sixteen-row transition matrix
completed unit-equivalent work is preserved across every recognized model transition without a redundant runtime mutation
current research exact level fractional progress queue and completed levels are preserved
configuration change save reload and a second reload are idempotent
continuous execution equals save reload execution
unknown or over-budget descriptors fail closed without guessing
default behavior remains equivalent to public 3.2.3 except for the named correction
Factorio 2.0 receives an explicit target disposition and independent proof

closure.development_result: passed direct five-archetype 3.2.3-to-3.2.5 upgrade and Space Age native-owner settings configuration change without a redundant second conversion
closure.proof_required: exact 3.2.3 default parity, configuration-change and reload equivalence, idempotence, exact candidate engine realization, and Factorio 2.0 target disposition before candidate freeze
